article_title: Opossum Cathelicidins Exhibit Antimicrobial Activity Against a Broad Spectrum of Pathogens Including West Nile Virus

mechanism_summary.bacterial_mechanism_topline: The paper directly supports bacterial membrane permeabilization/disruption for ΔModoCath1, ΔModoCath5, and ΔModoCath6 by dual-dye assays, with additional FE-SEM envelope-damage evidence for ΔModoCath1 and ΔModoCath5 and CD/LPS conformation evidence for ΔModoCath1 and ΔModoCath5.
mechanism_summary.antiviral_mechanism_topline: ΔModoCath5 inhibits WNV replication in keratinocytes, but the paper explicitly leaves the antiviral mechanism undefined; direct virucidal testing and measured antiviral-response modulation were negative at the tested condition.
downgrade_notes: MIC, serum/salt/pH stability, cytotoxicity, and WNV viral-load reduction are phenotype-supported rather than direct mechanism closure.
DBAASP/AMPA/PSIPRED antimicrobial-core and secondary-structure predictions remain computational_only or inferred_mechanism support, not direct mechanism evidence.
Do not curate ΔModoCath5 WNV inhibition as direct virion inactivation or immune-response upregulation.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: ΔModoCath1 and ΔModoCath5 interact with E. coli LPS in a way that induces or strengthens α-helical conformation, supporting bacterial surface/membrane engagement but not by itself proving cell killing.
direct_assay_types: circular dichroism spectroscopy with E. coli LPS titration
source_locators: paper.xml::sec[title='Secondary Structure Formation of ΔModoCath1 and 5 After Interaction With E. coli LPS']
paper.pdf text: Secondary Structure Formation of ΔModoCath1 and 5 After Interaction With E. coli LPS
mechanism_claims.evidence_notes: The method used 25 μM peptides and increasing LPS concentrations (0-0.16 mg/mL), subtracting the LPS spectrum. Results report increasing helicity for both peptides on LPS exposure; ΔModoCath5 already showed helical signal in aqueous solution.
mechanism_claims.strength_notes: Direct biophysical evidence for LPS-associated conformational change. It supports a membrane-interaction model but should be combined with dye/SEM evidence before asserting membrane disruption. No target receptor, enzyme, DNA/RNA, or intracellular binding target is demonstrated.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: ΔModoCath1, ΔModoCath5, and ΔModoCath6 increase bacterial membrane permeability and disrupt membrane potential in B. cereus, E. coli, and S. aureus under the dual-dye assay.
source_locators: paper.xml::sec[title='Disruption of Bacterial Membrane Permeability by ModoCaths']
paper.pdf text: Disruption of Bacterial Membrane Permeability by ModoCaths
mechanism_claims.evidence_notes: Cells were treated at 0.1x, 0.2x, and 1x MIC, with nisin and vancomycin controls. The paper reports increased TO-PRO-3 and DiOC2(3) fluorescence after treatment with all three tested peptides across B. cereus, E. coli, and S. aureus.
mechanism_claims.strength_notes: This is the strongest direct mechanism evidence for all three peptides: dye entry indicates membrane permeability damage and DiOC2(3) signal indicates membrane-potential disruption. It supports membrane disruption as an antibacterial mechanism, but it does not distinguish a pore architecture, molecular target, or downstream intracellular pathway.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: ΔModoCath1 and ΔModoCath5 cause visible E. coli envelope damage, pores/blisters, and cytoplasmic leakage after exposure at 2x MIC.
direct_assay_types: field-emission scanning electron microscopy of treated E. coli
source_locators: paper.xml::sec[title='Damage to Bacterial Cell Envelop and Leakage of Cell Contents Following Exposure to ModoCaths']
paper.pdf text: Damage to Bacterial Cell Envelop and Leakage of Cell Contents Following Exposure to ModoCaths
mechanism_claims.evidence_notes: E. coli ATCC 25922 was treated for 2 or 4 h with 1.5 μg/mL ΔModoCath1 or 10 μg/mL ΔModoCath5; PMAP36 and untreated cells were controls. The text describes complete or partial membrane disruption, pores, blisters, and leakage of cytoplasmic material.
mechanism_claims.strength_notes: Direct morphology evidence reinforces the membrane-disruption mechanism for ΔModoCath1 and ΔModoCath5. It does not cover ΔModoCath6 and does not identify a precise pore structure or non-membrane target.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: ΔModoCath5 reduces WNV replication in primary human keratinocytes at 16 μg/mL, while ΔModoCath1 and ΔModoCath6 do not show antiviral effects in the tested setup.
source_locators: paper.xml::sec[title='Strong Inhibition of West Nile Virus Replication by ΔModoCath5']
paper.pdf text: Strong Inhibition of West Nile Virus Replication by ΔModoCath5
mechanism_claims.evidence_notes: Keratinocytes were treated with peptide at 16 μg/mL before WNV infection at MOI 0.1 for 24 h. Viral RNA in supernatant decreased about 500-fold with ΔModoCath5, and cell monolayer viral load decreased about 1 log/93%; ΔModoCath1 and ΔModoCath6 were reported inactive in this antiviral assay.
mechanism_claims.strength_notes: This is antiviral phenotype evidence, not direct mechanism evidence. It should be curated as WNV replication inhibition by ΔModoCath5 with mechanism unresolved.

absence_and_boundary_notes: No direct enzyme, receptor, ribosome, DNA/RNA-binding, pull-down, SPR, ITC, NMR, docking/MD-validated target, or intracellular target assay was found in the source packet.
No direct virucidal effect of any tested ModoCath peptide on WNV was observed at 16 μg/mL for 1 h in the pre-incubation assay.
The paper does not close the mechanism of ΔModoCath5 antiviral activity; it explicitly states that the mechanism remains to be defined.
The bacterial mechanism should be recorded as membrane permeability/potential disruption and envelope damage, not as a specific molecular pore architecture.

adjudicator_summary: Bacterial mechanism is source-supported as membrane permeability/potential disruption for all three tested peptides, with CD/LPS and FE-SEM support for ΔModoCath1/5. ΔModoCath5 antiviral activity is phenotype-supported only; direct virucidal and measured antiviral-response modulation tests are negative/cautionary, so WNV mechanism remains unresolved.
